items.check: No doc_diff addition uses change-relative language (previously, now, no longer, added, removed, used to, formerly, the change or tier 'removes', the stats block 'gains')

The test_splice.py section comment does not describe the edit ('the thing the tier removes', guards 'left on' a fixture, 'an editorial one still aborting') but states what each guard asserts as it stands
The SpliceResult and assemble_output docstring additions read as present-state description; 'an aborted run is still a run' is within-run reasoning rather than change-relative
Every DL-XXX cited in a doc_diff exists in traktor_nml/README.md and says what the citing sentence claims it says

preview_report's 'empty labels reads each winner as its input index ... rather than an IndexError' is cited to DL-150, which is about candidate keying and a pick storing the lowest-index contributor and says nothing about labels or an IndexError
'an empty card or a sentence reading 0 is what the wording rules refuse' is cited to DL-215 and DL-233; DL-233 states noun-count agreement, not a refusal of a zero count or an empty card
The contrast paragraph's citation is corrected from DL-310 to DL-308, and DL-308's stated reasoning is in fact the Traktor-against-Traktor contrast rather than the conflict-raising rule
theme.py's 'a second class for one panel would be a second definition of the same rule' is supported by DL-078 (one definition, not repeated at a call site) and DL-188 (a call site names a class)

The README doc_diff brings the DL-312 entry into line with the pair correction: the entry says SettledRow carries 'the primary key of the record whose values the output carries' while SettledRow.winner is an (input index, primary key) pair and CC-M-005-002's doc_diff corrects the identical phrase in traktor_nml/CLAUDE.md, leaving the decision-log authority contradicting the module map
No decision from planning_context.decisions is left undocumented; DL-315, DL-316 and DL-317 appear only in the README diff and in no doc_diff
A doc_diff states at draw() that a bound on it is deliberately out of this work's scope (DL-315), so a reader meets the decision where it binds rather than only in the README
The reconnect_timeout decision (DL-316) is documented where __main__.py's ui.run call is described, not only as a README entry
Every code_change carrying a diff carries a non-empty doc_diff (22 of 22 at iteration 1)
Each doc_diff is a well-formed overlay: --- a/ and +++ b/ naming the same path as the code_change's file, with context lines matching the post-diff state of that file

The removal line quotes the gui/CLAUDE.md reconstruct_report.py row as it stands after the code diff (preview_report(stats, groups, decisions, settled_rows)); the repository row reads preview_report(stats, groups, decisions), so the overlay must be anchored to post-diff text
The removal line quotes the traktor_nml/CLAUDE.md splice.py row exactly as CC-M-005-002's own diff writes it, so the pair correction replaces text that exists
No doc_diff addition flips a file's line endings: app.py, traktor_nml/CLAUDE.md, tests/CLAUDE.md and docs/CLAUDE.md are CRLF; theme.py, splice.py, metadata_tier.py and tests/ are LF
Added comments and docstrings give the reason rather than restating the code
SettledRow.is_outlier's docstring explains why the readings are read off the row rather than describing that it returns bool(self.outliers)
PreviewReport.outlier_count's docstring explains why it counts readings rather than groups
OutlierRow._read's docstring explains why the raw string leads rather than describing the f-string
No doc_diff describes the tier as the same idea as matching.py's tolerant verification or as sharing its tolerance; matching.py is cited for contrast only

No doc_diff documents the new rule as covering a re-encode to a new extension: a changed filename changes the LOCATION and the primary key, so it is a dangling entry rather than a conflict or a settled group
Every doc_diff describing the outlier listing calls it a reading rather than a row to decide, and none describes a settled group as also being a conflict
Each test-file doc_diff records the specific mutation and the verbatim observed output convention, and states the paired-guard requirement where a band is asserted (DL-189)
The band's paired guards are documented with the two values read off the real collection pair, and the pairing is justified as closing the guard-green-in-exactly-the-broken-state case
No doc_diff cites a line number or quoted source text the named file does not carry (splice.py:341 and :52, matching.py:120-150, model.py:66-96, app.py:2661)
Where two code_changes overlay the same file, their doc_diff additions agree with each other and neither states a rule the other contradicts
Any doc_diff wording that names a count routes its plural through gui/wording.plural and describes the count as read off the model (DL-215)
No doc_diff writes into docs/plans/, and the docs/ record's date and name match the milestone that produces it
Hunk headers use the planner's prose-anchor convention consistently across all 22 doc_diffs rather than mixing prose anchors with line-range headers
The rewritten contrast paragraph does not cite DL-308 twice in one sentence where one citation carries it
